passages.title: Promising Early Results
passages.text: Although the proposal appears practical, its success depends on assumptions that have not yet been tested. We should therefore distinguish between promising early results and evidence of lasting improvement.
passages.levelRationale: The argument qualifies an initial judgment and distinguishes between related kinds of evidence.

passages.title: Interpreting Public Data
passages.text: Public data can reveal meaningful patterns, provided we remember that measurement choices shape the picture we see. A persuasive chart may clarify a trend, yet still conceal uncertainty or exclude relevant experience.
passages.levelRationale: The passage develops a qualified abstract claim about interpretation and hidden limitations.

passages.title: The Appearance of Efficiency
passages.text: A shorter meeting may appear more efficient, but speed alone is a poor measure of progress. If unresolved concerns merely resurface later, the saved time is largely an illusion.
passages.levelRationale: The passage challenges a superficial measure and develops its qualification through a hypothetical consequence.

passages.title: Travel and Restoration
passages.text: Travel is often presented as an escape from routine, though unfamiliar places can be demanding in their own way. Its restorative value may lie less in comfort than in renewed attention.
passages.levelRationale: An abstract reflection reframes a familiar idea through concession and precise comparison.

Effective leadership is often associated with confident speech, though listening may shape outcomes just as powerfully.
The capacity to tolerate dissent, rather than merely invite it, can determine whether a team thinks independently.

chunks.text: Photographs promise to preserve experience, yet constant documentation can subtly alter what we remember.
When attention shifts toward future viewing, the present moment may be observed less fully than it is recorded.

chunks.text: Trust in workplaces is rarely built through stated values alone, however prominently they are displayed.
It emerges more reliably from predictable responses, especially when deadlines slip or disagreements become uncomfortable.

chunks.text: Living by the seasons is sometimes dismissed as nostalgia, although it can be a practical response to excess.
Accepting limits on availability may restore a sense of proportion that constant access quietly erodes.

chunks.text: Language change is often lamented as decline, yet such judgments usually reflect familiarity rather than logic.
What sounds imprecise today may, with sustained use, acquire distinctions that current rules cannot easily express.

chunks.text: The pursuit of comfort can masquerade as prudence, even when it narrows the range of possible growth.
Taking modest, reversible risks may therefore preserve security better than avoiding uncertainty altogether.

A sheltered courtyard or early morning hour may reveal patterns of life that daytime noise otherwise obscures.
